title: What If You Could Stop Time for 10 Seconds a Day?

facts.claim: Usain Bolt ran 100 metres in 9.58 seconds (world record)
facts.source: World Athletics Championships, Berlin, 16 Aug 2009; Guinness World Records 'Fastest run 100 metres (male)'

facts.claim: Light travels about 3 million kilometres in 10 seconds
facts.source: Speed of light in vacuum is exactly 299,792,458 m/s (SI definition, BIPM); x10 s = 2,997,925 km

lines.text: Gym class, 10:14 a.m. A dodgeball is 4 inches from your face. And it's not moving.
Neither is anyone else. Not the teacher. Not the kid who threw it. Not the fly above his head.
Okay. Okay okay okay.
In the corner of your eye, a clock you've never seen before is counting down. 7.2 seconds.
So you step to the side. You turn the ball around. And you aim it back at the kid who threw it.
Time starts again.
Bro. What did I just watch?
Starting today, you get 10 seconds a day where the whole world stops. In the next month, you'll go viral, get offered 1 million dollars, and find out what 10 seconds are really worth.
The rules. 10 seconds a day, total. You can use them all at once, or in tiny pieces. At midnight, the clock refills.
Anything you touch can move. Anything you don't stays frozen.
10 seconds doesn't sound like much. But in 2009, Usain Bolt ran 100 meters in 9.58. In 10 seconds, light travels about 3 million kilometers.
You? You use your first full second to take the last slice of pizza out of your dad's hand.
Where did the pizza go?
By Wednesday you're getting good at it.
Half a second to catch your phone before it hits the floor. 2 seconds to finish the last question before the bell. 1 second to be first in the lunch line, every single day.
Then, on the stairs, Ava drops her phone. 3 floors down.
0.8 seconds later, it's back in her hand.
Wait. How did you...?
Reflexes.
That night, YouTube shows you a Zach King video. A guy who makes magic look real, with editing.
Millions of people watch him and ask the same thing. How did he do that?
Your tricks don't need editing.
So I film, you do the magic, we split everything. 50 50.
Video 1. You ask a stranger to sign a card. 1.4 seconds later, the card is inside a sealed water bottle in her own bag.
24 hours later: 3 million views. The top comment says fake. The second says edited.
So you go live. No cuts. 200,000 people watching. You make every coin in a fountain jump into one stranger's hat.
We're trending. We are actually trending.
Brand deals start showing up. 5,000 dollars a video. Then 20,000. Your mom asks if you're selling something illegal.
Then the email that changes everything.
The biggest live New Year's show in the country. One impossible trick, live, at 11:59 p.m. If the whole stadium can't explain it, you win 1 million dollars.
You plan the trick. 60,000 phones. Every single one ends up in one giant pile on stage. It takes exactly 9 seconds.
So on December 31st, you don't use a single second. Not for pizza. Not for the bus. 10.0, all day.
7:40 p.m. On the way to the stadium, a little kid chases his ball into the street.
And a bus is coming. Too fast to stop.
You know what happens if you use your seconds. No 9 seconds, no trick. No trick, no million.
You stop time anyway.
You walk into the street, lift the kid, carry him to the sidewalk, and put the ball back in his hands. 6.6 seconds.
Time starts again. The bus roars past an empty street. 3.4 seconds left.
11:58 p.m. 60,000 people. Cameras everywhere. You walk on stage with 3.4 seconds.
Ladies and gentlemen, the kid everyone says is impossible!
Bro, what are you doing? We need 9 seconds!
You look at the giant clock above the stadium. 11:59 and 50 seconds.
And you remember the rule. At midnight, the clock refills.
Can everyone help me count down?
3! 2! 1! Happy New Year!
10.0. You stop time.
You run row by row. Phone, phone, phone. 60,000 of them. 9 seconds.
Time starts again. 60,000 people reach for their phones to film the fireworks. And every single phone is on the stage, in one giant pile, under your feet.
The stadium goes silent. Then it explodes.
1 million dollars. Half for Theo.
But the video that breaks the internet isn't the trick. It's a dashcam from the bus. A kid in the street, and then, one frame later, on the sidewalk. 90 million views.
You teleported a kid and didn't tell me?
Outside the stadium, Ava is waiting.
Okay. You owe me the truth. How do you really do it?
Give me 10 seconds.
You stop time. And you spend all 10 seconds deciding what to say.
So, if you got 10 seconds a day where the whole world stops, what would you use them for? Tell me in the comments.
